subject: Acme renewal & expansion recap
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 1 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: Renewal & expansion conversation (usage, goals, next steps)

Hi Alex / Priya,

Thanks again for taking the time today — appreciated the candid discussion. Below is a quick recap to make sure we’re aligned and capture next steps. Let me know if I missed anything.

Summary of the call
- Current state: Acme is on Redwood Hosted API (standard tier). Monthly token usage ~1.2B tokens with a 20% month-over-month growth trend.
- Pain points: 1) rising unit costs for high-volume batches, 2) latency spikes during peak ingest events, 3) lack of per-route cost visibility for different product teams.
- Goals: reduce per-token cost by ~30% at current scale, keep 99th pct latency under 150ms for customer-facing workloads, and enable per-team routing/quotas. Also evaluate private/dedicated options for sensitive workflows.
- Potential upsell: Dedicated reserved capacity for inference + Redwood Optimize recommendations (batching + quantization) to hit cost/latency targets.

Usage notes we reviewed
- Jul 2026: 1.2B tokens (80% generation, 20% embedding).
- Peak window: 8–10am PST, sustained high concurrency during product launch test.

Proposed timeline
- Week of Aug 9: Deep-dive technical workshop (Vivek + infra team) to scope Dedicated config and network requirements.
- Aug 16: Draft proposal including SLOs, pricing for reserved capacity, and migration plan.
- Sep 1: Target decision date for renewal + expansion to start in Oct.

Immediate next steps
1) I’ll share the draft proposal and the July usage export (attached).
2) Vivek to propose dates for the technical workshop.
3) Alex/Priya to confirm stakeholders for procurement and security review.

Attachments: ACME_Renewal_Proposal_v3.pdf (proposal draft), Usage_Report_Jul2026.csv (usage export)

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

On Fri, 31 Jul 2026 09:07:00 -0700, Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com> wrote:
> Thanks Marissa — that summary looks good. A couple of clarifications:
> - The 1.2B tokens number includes internal QA traffic (about ~15%). We should show both gross and net for procurement.
> - Security will likely want a quick checklist for data residency and KMS integrations.
>
> Alex

Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 10:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: Renewal & expansion conversation (usage, goals, next steps)

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the recap — confirms what we discussed. A few quick notes:
- We’ll strip out QA traffic for the procurement-facing numbers; gross vs net is important for budgeting.
- For the technical workshop please include networking (VPC peering), KMS options, and any requirements for on-prem connectors — security will need that checklist.
- Tentative stakeholders: Priya (sec), Samir Patel (procurement), and Lina Gomez (platform).

I’m available Aug 10–12 for the technical workshop window.

Regards,
Alex
